facts.md (484 lines) has six sections: conventions, timeline, render cost, close-up quality, camera geometry and lighting, plus an ATC-audio section for the owner's request. Every figure was read from the replay data or the app's own state, or measured in renders on the v5 Full build. Inferences are marked [inf]. Stills and contact sheets are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/wf/film/explore/ and benchmark JSON/logs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/3fd08d73-28ea-592f-8f33-69ede4de867b/scratchpad/wf/film/bench/. Large intermediates (mp4 files, full-size PNGs) were deleted and the close-up stills converted to JPEG.

**1. Timeline (T = s after F0 20:45:58.662Z).**
- Raw ADS-B:
  - Push-back about 232.5-328; a further 72 m forward roll from 328 to 381; stationary until about 637.
  - Taxi starts about 637-639, with stops at 684-746 and 1279-1405.
  - Holds short of 28R from 1601 to 1725, lines up 1725-1787.5, then sits at the displaced threshold.
  - Brake release 1802.2 (21:16:00.9Z). Speeds of 20/40/60/80/100/120/140/160/180 kt are timed, and lift-off is about 1847.3 at about 2300 m along the runway.
  - 500/1000/2000 ft AGL at 1863.5/1874.3/1896.8.
- The app's display:
  - Roll starts 1806.78, rotation 1840.79 (8 deg reached at 1845.54), lift-off 1847.41.
  - Gear retracts 1851.41-1858.41; flaps 1897-1901.
  - The tables include positions (x, y, z), main-gear position, heading, speed, pitch, gear and flaps, plus the gate, push and taxi phases.
- Other traffic: a B788 crosses the 28L threshold at the moment of UAL857's lift-off, and a China Airlines 777 is at the hold behind it.

**2. Render cost.**
- Seconds per frame and survival:
  - 1080p high, hi livery: 2.08 s/frame, survived 220 frames.
  - 1440p: 3.10 s/frame, survived 220.
  - 4K: 8.2 s/frame; the renderer was killed by the out-of-memory killer at about frame 66.
  - 4x sub-frame accumulation at 1080p: 11.4 s per output frame. It works with TRAA (no ghosting; the background turns into a box-shutter streak).
  - Terminal orbit at 1080p: 2.08 s/frame, survived 220 frames.
- The real memory ceiling is a 14.34 GB limit shared by every workflow's shell commands, not the 15.7 GB of RAM. The Chromium GPU process grows about 10 MB for every frame the virtual clock advances, so the rule is at most about 200 frames per browser session.
- `&res=1` is needed for anything above 1080p; record3 does not pass it today.
- The v5 build forces the 512-px (`lo`) livery; the v2 films used it too.
- Draws of the same shot drifted by up to 3.2 s between runs.
- Recommendation: 1440p, high tier, hi livery, about 5-5.5 h for 3600 frames. Use accumulation only on selected fast shots. 4K and the ultra/hybrid tiers are not recommended.

**3. Close-up limits (1080p, vfov 30, hi livery).** Nose gear, engines and wing hold up from 10 m, the main truck from 15-20 m, the fin globe from 30-40 m, the cockpit from 15-20 m and the registration from 8-10 m. Frame gear retraction from 25-30 m. The gear rig folds rigidly and there are no wheel wells.

**4. Camera.**
- Limits:
  - The floor is 2.5 m above ground and there is no collision test.
  - Roll is impossible and the fov is vertical.
- record3 lacks:
  - multi-key moves
  - aircraft-local look-at points or mounts
  - dolly-zoom
  - roll
  - variable speed within a shot
  - deterministic resume
- Vantage points: tower eye at (-739.0, 62.15, 323.5), with lift-off at 871 m on bearing 22 deg and the G13 gate blocked by the ITB roof. Also the G-pier roof, ground positions near 28R, and speed envelopes for camera platforms.

**5. Lighting.** The film sun is az 238.4, el 11.3, 60 deg left of the nose, so the left side is lit. The sun is in frame at yawOff about 120 deg. The engine has no lens-flare effect.

**6. ATC audio.** The section gives UTC times, frequencies and the LiveATC terms; nothing was retrieved.

A script checked every one of the 3,660 frames against the measured limits in facts.md, and no warnings remain. The limits checked were:
- the minimum framing for each detail (cockpit, gear, fin, registration);
- the registration decal, which is only drawn within 350 m of the camera;

**Deliverables:** a 1440p master and a 1080p phone version. The owner says they cannot download on their phone, so the plan also includes an HLS streaming page.

**Sound:** the film works with music alone. The music starts 22.5 s in, so its A chord lands on the frame where the wheels leave. Six optional ATC slots are marked. **No engine change is needed.** The tooling changes the renderer needs are in md section 12: keyframes, aim points on the aircraft, zoom by subject size, per-range blur, a deterministic warm-up, chunked sessions, and checks that the drawn pose matches the data.

How the cut works:
- **Rhythm.** Detail, detail, then a wide (aerial, tower cab or long-lens ground camera). A minimap inset runs from push-back to gear-up so the viewer always knows where the aircraft is.
- **Timing.** Details land on the drawn events: crash zoom-out on the left main truck at brake release (1806.78), rotation 1840.79, wheels off 1847.41, gear doors opening 1851.9-1853.5 and closing 1856.5-1858.0, gear up 1858.41. The take-off shots carry an anchor: a probe pass measures the event and shifts the shot's clock so it lands on its frame.
- **What the 777 model can show.** I checked js/three/aircraft.js: the model animates only the gear legs and the belly doors. It has no nose-wheel steering, wheel or fan rotation, truck tilt, flaps, slats or control-surface motion (the app's flap setting draws nothing on this model). So:
  - the GE90 fan close-up is at the stand with the engines off;
  - the trucks are shown close only when stopped or seen from behind;
  - steering, tyre and engine facts appear as callouts sourced from Boeing's airport planning document (refs/cache/acap);
  - every frame is checked so a fan face never exceeds 50 px with engines running, and a turning wheel never exceeds 40 px when its hub faces the camera.
- **Camera checks, frame by frame.** Detail-size limits from facts.md, the registration-decal 350 m limit, LOD and shadow distance, sun in frame, building sight lines, runway/taxiway pavement, the aircraft's swept path, the vehicles placed around a parked aircraft at G13, the take-off jet blast read from the Boeing document (s.6.1.12), platform speeds and other traffic. No flags remain except a 45 %-chance catering truck that could block d01; an alternate camera position is specified.
- **Render.** 2560x1440, high tier, `&fixedres=1&res=1`, hi livery, TRAA, 180-deg shutter, motion-blur sub-frames only where the background streaks more than 8 px. The 1080p version is a 1.78x supersampled downscale. Cost: 5,627 rendered frames in 50 browser sessions, about 570 min (9.5 h) on the render lock, plus a preview pass of about 2 h. Fallbacks save 47 and 21 min.
- **Sound.** It works with music.wav alone. Offset 12.66 s puts the E-to-A chord change on the frame where the wheels leave. Seven optional ATC slots are marked: in sync where a real-time shot covers the call, labelled excerpts otherwise, with the music ducked -12 dB under speech.
- **Delivery.** You said you can't download on mobile, so the film is planned as an HLS streaming page you open by link, plus a 1080p faststart MP4. The 1440p master stays on disk.
- **No repo or engine change is needed.** One optional render-quality change (an in-page motion-blur buffer behind `?acc=n`) is listed but not assumed in the budget.

findings.title: Decision (c) not met: fast ranges outside f13/f19/f22 render with n=2-5, so discrete copies 13-58 px apart
findings.evidence: I used a camera-motion model (rev2t/blur.cjs, blur_f24.cjs) calibrated against r2c's observed copy spacing (23 px for f24 180-203 at n=8, 9 px for f13). At 1440p it predicts: f18_tower_crash v1-3 at n=2 with a crash zoom of 215 px/frame at r=300 px, copies up to 58 px apart (frame 38), 37 frames over 6 px; f23_rotate n=2/3, 215 frames over 6 px (worst 16.1 px, frame 7); f26_gear n=2/3, 59 frames (18.5 px); f08_hold n=3, 58 frames (13.4 px); f16 n=2, 6 frames (12.6 px). f24 v0-7 is n=5 because of the 1-ms cap (filmcam.cjs:179-181 accN), giving 19-21 px copies. The worst f24 frame is 172 (v 7.17, 26.7 px). That is inside the v7-8.5 'n=20' ramp, but accN caps it to 5-6 because the speed there is only about 0.25-0.3x. So the r2c claim 'n=20 at the f24 peak' misses the worst frames. My s6 run (f24 130-135 at 2560x1440, n=5, at wheels-off) showed no visible copies, but only because the background in that window is featureless: |dI/dx| <= 0.7 in the pavement band, and the autocorrelation peaks are inconclusive. Root cause: the cap is justified by Date.now's 1-ms resolution for traffic.update, but film.mjs:424-425 computes the camera (filmOf) at the continuous sub-time vs[k]. Only page.clock.runFor is quantised.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive n per frame from the measured screen motion, including zoom at the frame corners, with a target of 6 px or less between copies. Set n>=8 for f18 v1-3, f23, f26 v5.6-8.0, f08 and f16's fast tail. Lift the 1-ms cap for camera motion: keep the camera sub-steps continuous and let consecutive sub-steps reuse the same traffic millisecond (or add a sub-ms clock shim behind a URL parameter). Then re-test f24 frames 165-180 and f18 30-44 at 1440p and look at crops of textured background.

findings.title: f24 1/4x lift-off close-up shows the 777 main-gear wheels not turning at ~185 kt
findings.evidence: In s6 (f24 frames 130-135 at 1440p, rev2t/s6_wheel.png and s6_sheet.png), the 20-spoke hubs and the polygonal tyre facets have the same orientation in all six frames and are crisp in every n=5 ACC frame. At 95 m/s a ~1.3 m tyre turns about 22 rev/s: 85 deg per output frame at 1/4x and about 42 deg during the 180-deg shutter, so a real camera would show the spokes heavily smeared. js/three/aircraft.js has gear retraction (uGearT) and no wheel spin. The aircraft is drawn airborne from T 1847.375, so this window is the wheels-off moment of the hero shot. Decision (f) puts engine and scene issues out of scope, but the shot design is what makes this visible, and it breaks the owner's physical-plausibility rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a URL-gated wheel spin (rotate the zone 3/4 wheel vertices about the axle by the integral of gs/r while on the ground; a small engine change behind a URL parameter, as the constraints allow) and render that range with enough sub-steps, or reframe/re-time f24 so the wheels are not the slow-motion subject. Check f13/f23 for the same exposure.

findings.title: check_cameras gate can be bypassed: platform whitelist, drones exempt from the RSA, no ROFA/TSA, mask-only buildings without line of sight
findings.evidence: The ground rules (water, pavement, RSA, MAX_AGL) apply only to names in GROUND_PLATFORMS/MAX_AGL (check_cameras.mjs:88, 98, 133, 137, 152), and platform names are never validated: 'Tripod', a typo or a new name skips every ground rule. Drone, heli_low, heli and jet (9 shots) are exempt from the RSA: f15 (drone) sits at lateral -75 m, inside the 76.2 m RSA half-width, at 8 m AGL during the take-off roll and passes. There is no TSA/TOFA/ROFA test, so an adversarial tripod 3 m off a taxiway edge passes and 14 shot-list cameras are inside the D-V ROFA. Scene-extra mask buildings are tested only for agl<25 and never for line of sight. The airframe model is coarse (fin/stab chord, no dihedral). The RENDER_LOGS re-check (lines 179-188) covers only AGL and RSA.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail on unknown platforms. Apply the RSA/ROFA to drones and helicopters, or give those shots an honesty label (e.g. 'drone position not operationally possible during an active take-off'). Add TSA/TOFA half-widths for ground platforms, a line-of-sight test against mask cells, and run every rule again on the rendered logs.

findings.title: First output frame of a resumed chunk differs visibly from a one-session render (TRAA history)
findings.evidence: Poses are bit-identical across resume and across resolutions (0.000 m, s3 vs s5, f14_rear 3-5 at 720p). The diff (rev2t/resume_diff_f3.png) is edge-only, and a distant aircraft's centroid moves by <0.8 px, so this is TRAA history/jitter phase, not position. It can show as a one-frame shimmer at chunk joins.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw more frames before a resumed chunk's first output frame (RESUME_DRAW>=4) and match the TRAA jitter index to the frame number, or have plan.py place chunk boundaries at cuts or low-detail frames.

findings.title: session.sh takes the exit code from the last 'SESSION END' in a log that may hold an earlier run
findings.evidence: session.sh appends to LOG (>>), then reads rc from the last 'SESSION END ... exit N' line (and checks for 'PROBE DONE'). run.sh names logs p${pass}_s$i.log and restarts pass numbering on every invocation. If a re-run session dies before writing SESSION END, it reports the earlier run's code, and estimate.py parses duplicated lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Truncate the LOG or write a per-session marker, and read rc only after that marker.
